about.title: About Bumelerze
about.intro: Bumelerze grew out of years of earthquake research in Kurdistan. It brings trusted earthquake data together and shows it in Sorani, Kurmanji, Arabic and English. It is free, has no ads, and does not sell data.
about.why: When the ground shakes here, people search for news in their own language and often find rumours. Bumelerze answers with named sources, in plain words, and asks what you felt so the shaking can be mapped. Earthquakes cannot be predicted. This app reports what has happened.
about.fake_tip1: The real app is only at bumelerze.com/app. It is not in any app store yet.
about.fake_tip2: Bumelerze never predicts earthquakes. Any message that predicts one is not from Bumelerze.
about.fake_tip3: Bumelerze is free. It never asks for money, card details or passwords.

hiw.meta.title: How Bumelerze works: data, SHAKEmaps, damage estimates
hiw.meta.description: Where Bumelerze gets its earthquake data, how it makes SHAKEmaps and damage estimates for Iraq, and how your reports help.
hiw.title: How Bumelerze works
hiw.intro: Bumelerze brings trusted earthquake data together, maps the shaking, and estimates likely damage. Here is how each part works, and where its limits are.
hiw.data.headline: Where the data comes from
hiw.data.body: Live earthquakes come from three networks: USGS, EMSC and GEOFON. The catalogue holds 150,072 earthquakes since the year 872, from six catalogues: ISC, ISC-GEM, EMME, Onur 2017, KISC and USGS. Each earthquake is merged and shown once, with its sources.
hiw.shakemaps.headline: SHAKEmaps, made by Bumelerze
hiw.shakemaps.body: A SHAKEmap shows how strongly the ground shook in each place. Bumelerze computes its own for earthquakes in Iraq or felt in Kurdistan, from ground-motion models, nearby seismic stations and people's reports. Each map is labelled automatic or reviewed.
hiw.damage.headline: Damage estimates for Iraq
hiw.damage.body: Probabilistic models combine the mapped shaking with Iraq's building stock and its vulnerability classes to estimate likely damage to buildings. These are estimates, not certainties. They cover Iraq only.
hiw.reports.headline: Your reports improve the maps
hiw.reports.body: To share your experience, tap the picture closest to what you felt. No account is needed. Reports are grouped by area into community intensity, which helps improve the SHAKEmaps.
hiw.building.headline: Know your building's class
hiw.building.body: Tag my building asks plain questions about your home. It returns the building type, a vulnerability class from A to F, likely damage in strong shaking, and practical tips. It is a guide, not an engineer's inspection.
hiw.community.headline: Community, if you want it
hiw.community.body: Accounts are optional. With one, you can join event hubs, comment, and share what you felt with others. Hubs and comments are moderated. You can download your data or delete your account at any time.
hiw.next.headline: What comes next
hiw.next.body: Alerts about recorded earthquakes are coming soon. Early warning, a warning before strong shaking arrives, is a longer-term aim that Bumelerze works towards. It is not available today. Earthquakes cannot be predicted, and Bumelerze never claims to.
hiw.damage.alt: The app's page for one earthquake, with its estimated building damage.
hiw.flow.caption: How the parts connect: three networks feed one merged list, which drives the SHAKEmaps; felt reports also feed the SHAKEmaps, and the SHAKEmaps drive the damage estimates.
